bridge: Builds on B04 container versus VM boundaries, F03 confinement and D03 workload identity.
teaching:
A container packages a process environment but commonly shares the host kernel. Its risk depends on configuration: privileged mode, host mounts, capabilities and exposed sockets can grant substantial host authority. An image label is not a complete security boundary.

Workload identity determines what a running application can do to external services. Separate build-time credentials, runtime identity and user identity. A read-only filesystem does not stop an overprivileged cloud credential from deleting remote objects.

Inspect configuration before launching a lab workload. Prefer narrow mounts, non-root execution where compatible, limited capabilities and explicit network/service exposure. Pin image provenance and maintain updates. Resource limits also matter to availability; an isolated process can still exhaust a shared host if no limits apply.
example:
Configuration review fixture
User: non-root app user
Filesystem: read-only except disposable /tmp
Mounts: one read-only training input; no home or Docker socket
Network: local-only required service
Credentials: read-only identity for one synthetic dataset
Limits: bounded memory/CPU and restart policy
Image: recorded source and immutable digest
explanation: The Docker socket would expose a powerful host-control interface, so mounting it is a significant boundary change. Non-root is useful but not sufficient if the process receives broad capabilities or host handles. Read-only input prevents mutation, not data disclosure.
exercise: Compare the fixture with a second configuration: root user, writable host home mount, broad cloud key and no resource limits. Identify four distinct consequences and propose a scoped repair for each.
solution: Consequences include host-file modification, secret exposure, remote overprivilege and host exhaustion. Remove broad mounts/keys, scope identity, reduce process authority and set/test limits. Link each repair to the actual exposure.
challenge: Write an inspect-before-run checklist with one legitimate-function test and three denied-operation expectations. Explain why a green image vulnerability scan does not prove runtime configuration is safe.
challenge_solution: Scanning packages does not establish safe mounts, capabilities, identity or network policy. Verify deployed configuration and the workload's effective authority, while retaining a working required task.
